key_insight: ServerBench tests whether coding agents can build specialized LLM serving systems that maximize latency-qualified token value per dollar of GPU cost.
engineering_relevance: Effective serving designs coordinate capacity improvements with load selection while preserving session dependencies, latency targets, and correctness.
method: Let agents implement and experimentally optimize complete serving systems against a shared dollars-per-dollar objective.
Use stateful workload replay to preserve session dependencies.
Independently verify submitted systems and compare them with serving baselines.
evidence_signal: Across 11 coding-agent models and three deployments, 22 of 33 runs produced verified systems and 13 beat the strongest baseline; Claude Sonnet 5.5 reached 2.97 dollars per dollar on Gemma E4B, 4.87× the vLLM reference.
watch_item: Optimization can introduce execution paths that require explicit verification, and 11 of 33 runs did not yield verified systems.
paper_title: ServerBench: How can your coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems?
